Get into the holiday spirit as you immerse yourself in the enchanting world of North Pole Nights on select evenings now through December 31. This extraordinary experience includes jolly characters, fun live shows, ice skating under the stars, festive food and drinks, magical light displays and much, much more! The following rides will be closed during this Signature Event: Rainbow Garden Round Boat Ride, Paddle Boats, and Sky Trail Monorail Once you’ve made the trek across Candy Cane Lane bridge, you’ll find yourself in the festive world of North Pole Village with a chance to meet some of Santa’s merry, mischievous elves! You’ll find plenty of beautiful light displays throughout the park. Be prepared to “ooh” and “ahh” as you walk through this festive 100-foot-long animated musical Tunnel of Lights! Have you been good this year? Stop by one of the North Pole Post Office locations to write down your perfect wish for Christmas, then put it in the mailbox to send to Santa! On December 12 & 13 only, enjoy a reading of Elephant Garlic Christmas by Ken Christopher followed by book signings and FREE books, plus FREE fresh garlic and Christopher Ranch tote bags. Eat, drink, and be merry during North Pole Nights! Discover delicious holiday treats, cozy warm beverages, and festive cocktails and mocktails throughout the park. Satisfy your holiday cravings with delicious seasonal treats and festive food throughout the park! Warm up with a delicious hot beverage from Skitter's Cozy Cabin, the perfect way to stay warm on a chilly winter night! Find festive mocktails, cocktails, and warm beverages at our 3 bars: Skitter's Cozy Cabin, Live Tonight Bar, and Merry & Mischief Bar. The North Pole is the perfect place to practice your ice skating skills! Stop by the ice rink as you cross Candy Cane Lane into the North Pole Village. Already have a pair of skates? Simply fill out a waiver to skate FREE! See our staff at the ice rink for more info. Add a little extra magic to your holiday season with a North Pole Nights Bubble Wand! Choose from two festive favorites, a cheerful Reindeer or a classic Nutcracker, and fill the air with holiday bubbles! December 19 & 20 | 5, 6 & 7 PM Back by popular demand! Gather your loved ones for a traditional holiday feast featuring roasted turkey, honey baked ham, garlic mashed potatoes, stuffing, and all the trimmings. Kids Under 12 Eat FREE! Tinsel the Tree is finally free to bust a move! Hop aboard a train ride through the beautiful redwood forest and join him as he tries out his new dance moves. Join the studio audience of this lively late-night talk show to hear the latest and greatest from Diva the Elf as she welcomes a very special rising star. Experience the magic of the holidays like never before! Meet our new friends Rudy the Polar Bear, Mrs. Claus, Tinsel the Tree, Skitter the Mouse and a band of Santa’s reindeer as they share their wishes with Santa Claus himself. title: Fandom Swap
description: Feel free to come by and drop off your stuff and leave, or if you'd like, you can stick around and see what other people bring in!
parentSummary: Feel free to come by and drop off your stuff and leave, or if you'd like, you can stick around and see what other people bring in!
sourceDescriptionRaw:
Did the fandom that used to be your absolute fave stop sparking joy for you?nbsp;Have you hopped multiple fandoms over the years? Are your old acrylic standees, figurines, keychain charms, pins, prints, or stickers taking up too much space for the things from your new fandoms? Did you just clean out your room and ended up with massive piles of non-recyclable fandom merch you no longer want?
Cambrian Branch Library has got you covered with Fandom Swap!
We meet on the last Sunday of every month from 2 to 4PM.nbsp;Come bring in your clean, gently-loved fandom merchandise to find them new homes andnbsp;keep them out of landfills! There's no need to stay for the full duration of thisnbsp;program either. Feel free to come by and drop off your stuff and leave, or if you'd like, you can stick around and see what other people bring in!
So come join us to clean out your fandom goodies,nbsp;meet fellow fans, or discover new fandoms!
Official and unofficial merch are welcome, but all materials must benbsp;rated PG-13 and under.
Selling is prohibited in this program.
ADA Accommodation Requests

description: A selection of queer reading materials will be available to browse and checkout.nbsp;In addition to light snacks and refreshments, we'll have craft supplies and a selection of cozy and found family reads highlighting queer characters and authors.\nWhile the intention of this program is to create a safe and comfortable space for patrons identifying as LGBTQ+, we welcome all participants and reading materials.

sourceDescriptionRaw:
Queer joy shall abound at the Queer Café!nbsp;
Let's grab our chunky knit sweaters, a warm cup of something pumpkin-spiced, and celebrate the fall season for November's Queer Cafe.nbsp;
Queer Cafe is annbsp;LGBTQ+ friendly space in our community room for folks to gather, read, craft, and chat. A selection of queer reading materials will be available to browse and checkout.nbsp;In addition to light snacks and refreshments, we'll have craft supplies and a selection of cozy and found family reads highlighting queer characters and authors.
While the intention of this program is to create a safe and comfortable space for patrons identifying as LGBTQ+, we welcome all participants and reading materials. ADA Accommodation Requests
Café Queer
¡La alegría queer estará presente en cada rincón del Café Queer!
¡Pongámonos nuestros suéteres gruesos de punto, disfrutemos de una bebida calientita con especias de calabaza y celebremos la temporada de otoño en el Café Queer de noviembre!
El Café Queer es un espacio acogedor para la comunidad LGBTQ+ en nuestra sala comunitaria, donde las personas pueden reunirse, leer, hacer manualidades y conversar. Habrá una selección de libros y otros materiales de lectura con temática LGBTQ+ disponibles para explorar y llevar en préstamo.
Además de bocadillos y bebidas ligeras, tendremos materiales para manualidades y una selección de lecturas reconfortantes, incluidas historias sobre familias elegidas, que destacan a personajes y autores LGBTQ+.
Se anima a las personas participantes a compartir y conocer a otros lectores con intereses similares, pero no se les pedirá que revelen su identidad ni sus preferencias de lectura.
Aunque el propósito de este programa es crear un espacio seguro y cómodo para las personas que se identifican como LGBTQ+, todas las personas y todos los materiales de lectura son bienvenidos.
Solicitudes de adaptaciones ADA

title: TeenHQ MakerSpace Studio
description: Up to 5 teens at a time can use the space to utilize our 3D printers, Poster Printer, GlowForge, Sewing Serger Machines, Cricut, Button Press, and miscellaneous craft supplies.
parentSummary: Up to 5 teens at a time can use the space to utilize our 3D printers, Poster Printer, GlowForge, Sewing Serger Machines, Cricut, Button Press, and miscellaneous craft supplies.
sourceDescriptionRaw:
Middle and high schoolers: Come explore the TeenHQ MakerSpace! Up to 5 teens at a time can use the space to utilize our 3D printers, Poster Printer, GlowForge, Sewing Serger Machines, Cricut, Button Press, and miscellaneous craft supplies. Work with our teen librarian to bring your idea to life. Each machine and other materials have limitations and time requirements. Please see below for more information. All services are provided for free to middle and high school (6-12 grade) students. Younger people and adults are not permitted in the area unless required to assist with a disability. 
Pre-registration is now in-person, beginning at 3:45PM on the day of the event. The first five teens are guaranteed space.The area is wheelchair accessible from the Children’s Room elevator. Other accommodations can be made available with request.nbsp;ADA Accommodation RequestsPlease note that each device requires time to set up, use, and complete whatever task you're wanting to use the space for. Be sure that you have enough time in your schedule to attend the program. Not all tasks may be completed before the end of the program and you may need to return to get your completed items or pause your task and restart at another studio session. We appreciate your patience and flexibility.
3D Printing: All requested prints must take less than 6.5 hours to print. All requested prints will need to be picked up at a later date. Contact information is required for notification of pick-up. 3D print quality and time needed to complete prints is not guaranteed. Multiple objects can be printed as long as the total time does not exceed 6.5 hours. 
Poster Printing: All prints must be assembled on a 2”x3” canvas and printed as a.png. Please see the regularly scheduled poster printing event for further details. One poster per teen per day. 
GlowForge: Create a custom engraved object. Object should follow similar guidelines to the Custom Keychain Program. Complexity of request is at the discretion of the librarian. 
Sewing Serger Machines: It is recommended that you bring your own fabric and thread if fabric is special or color is a factor. There are scrap material and thread available but we cannot guarantee material quality or availability. An iron and ironing board is also available 
Cricut: Basic Cricut supplies are available, such as construction and cardstock paper. If your project is specialized, such as requiring iron-on, you’ll need to bring your own materials. It is recommended that you know the requirements for any materials you provide. 
Button Press: TeenHQ offers two sizes of button presses. We cannot offer printing. If your bring your own printout of buttons, it must be printed on standard printer paper. Paper thicker than standard printer paper cannot be used on the button presses. All measurements below are diameter length in inches. 
Small Button Press: 1.25” Large Button Press: 2.25” Picture Size: 1.156” Cut Line: 1.629” Picture Size: 2.063” Cut Line: 2.625”

description: Just like the original, in The Hip Hop Nutcracker, Maria-Clara and the Nutcracker Prince go on a dream adventure battling a gang of mice, visiting the land of sweets and learning the lessons of the holiday season.
parentSummary: Just like the original, in The Hip Hop Nutcracker, Maria-Clara and the Nutcracker Prince go on a dream adventure battling a gang of mice, visiting the land of sweets and learning the lessons of the holiday season.
sourceDescriptionRaw: | Performances: December 2-3, 2026 | A holiday mash-up for the whole family, The Hip Hop Nutcracker returns for another spectacular tour. Directed and choreographed by Tony and Olivier Award-nominated Jennifer Weber, this contemporary dance spectacle is a re-mixed and re-imagined version of the classic, smashing hip hop dance and Tchaikovsky’s timeless music together into a heart-stirring and inspirational holiday event. The Hip Hop Nutcracker is brought to life by a powerhouse cast of a dozen all-star dancers, a DJ, a violinist, and MC Kurtis Blow, one of hip hop’s founding fathers, who opens the show with a short set. Just like the original, in The Hip Hop Nutcracker, Maria-Clara and the Nutcracker Prince go on a dream adventure battling a gang of mice, visiting the land of sweets and learning the lessons of the holiday season. Innovative digital graffiti and visuals transform the landscape of E.T.A. Hoffmann’s beloved story from traditional 19th Century Germany to the vibrant, diverse sights and sounds of contemporary New York City. Grab your family and friends and let the dynamic performers of The Hip Hop Nutcracker take you on a journey that celebrates love, community and the magic of the holiday season. Performances: ● Wed., December 2, 2026 @ 7:00pm ● Thur., December 3, 2026 @ 7:00pm > CPA Events Calendar > Visitor FAQs

title: Reading to Children in Japanese にほんご　おはなし会
description: Preschool age children and their parents/caregivers are invited to the West Valley Branch Library for Reading to Children in Japanese.
parentSummary: Preschool age children and their parents/caregivers are invited to the West Valley Branch Library for Reading to Children in Japanese.
sourceDescriptionRaw:
Preschool age children and their parents/caregivers are invited to the West Valley Branch Library for Reading to Children in Japanese. Every Thursday at 11:00 AM, children will enjoy early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities all in the Japanese language. 
This program is brought to the library by Poponta Children's Cultural Society. Established in 2008 and based in San Mateo, Poponta is comprised of a group of volunteers dedicated to serving the Japanese-speaking community. Poponta volunteers tell stories to children to open their minds to the magic of books. To learn more about Poponta, please visit:nbsp;https://ja-jp.facebook.com/popontanokai/
Free, with limited capacity. Seating is available on a first-come, first-served basis. A limited number of tickets will be distributed at the Information Desk 30 minutes prior to the start of the program. San José Public Library Early Education programs are in alignment with the City’s Education and Digital Literacy Initiative. 
 
ADA Accommodation Requests
 未就園児のお子さま、日本語に興味のあるお子さまとその保護者の皆さまは、ウェストバレーブランチ図書館日本語お話会にご参加いただけます。毎週木曜日の午前11時に、絵本の読みきかせ、手遊び歌、昔話、ペープサートなどが楽しめます。このプログラムは、ぽぽんた児童文化の会メンバーの一人と有志によって図書館で開催しています。 ぽぽんた児童文化の会は2008年に設立され、サンマテオを拠点とし、ベイエリアにお住まいの日本語を話すコミュニティに日本文化、日本語のお話を提供するボランティアグループです。パンデミック中の規則に準拠し、ストーリータイム(お話会)においてもいくつかルールが変更になりましたのでご確認ください。これは屋内プログラムになることに注意してください。全員（2歳以上）は屋内でマスク着用をお勧めします。座席は先着順でご利用いただけます。プログラム開始30分前にインフォメーションデスクにて、数量限定のチケットを配布いたします。サンノゼ公立図書館の早期教育プログラムは、市の教育およびデジタルリテラシーイニシアチブと連携しています。図書館主催のイベントでは、アメリカ障害者法に基づく介助が必要な場合、イベントの少なくとも7営業日前に408-244-4747にお電話ください。

Cash ChecksAll major Credit CardsApple Pay Google PayContactless payment available
Thursday, December 3nbsp;is members-only night. Doors open from 5:00pm until 8:00pm. For Thursday night access to the sale, enter at the rear (east side) of the library. You must have a valid membership card for entry, or purchase a membership at the door. Individual memberships allow 1 person to enter; family memberships allow the entire family to enjoy the book sale. sourceDescriptionRaw:
Write and Publish a Novel in a Year!
Join us for monthly writing and publishing workshops to push you through the process of crafting, finishing and publishing a novel/novella. Work independently to complete each month’s assigned word count, have one-on-one mentoring sessions, and exchange pages with your peers in a monthly critique group. Over the course of 12 months, you will create a book (minimum 17,500 words) and professionally publish it.
Completion of the novel/novella within the 12 month period is not mandatory, but If you complete your novel in the allotted timeframe, you will receive your own ISBN.
Registration required. Only 10 seats available!
To be eligible for an ISBN, one-on-one sessions, the critique group and to participate in the end of program Book Fair, you must register for the entire program. If you cannot make all of the sessions, but are registered and would like to remain eligible for all the perks,nbsp;you are responsible for keeping up with your monthly word commitment. You may join the program late, if there are still spaces available or someone leaves the program. So, joining the waiting list is very important, if it becomes an option.nbsp;nbsp;nbsp;
The critique group schedule and one-on-one sessions are TBD after the first workshop on November 7, 2026. You will receive individual invitations via email.nbsp;nbsp;

sourceDescriptionRaw: You applied for a job and received a call back for an interview. Congratulations! Do you want help preparing for the interview? Meet one-on-one with Daniel, an experienced job interview coach to help you prepare by giving feedback on your resume and conducting a mock interview. Sessions are one hour in length. Be prepared to share things with Daniel such as a current resume, the job position description you applied for, and if you can, come dressed as if you were going in to the actual interview. You must register for this event and registration ends the Thursday before the program. If you registered successfully, you will get a registration confirmation email with a link to pick your choice of time for this Saturday's program. Each session is one hour (15-30 minutes for interviewing + 30-45 minutes for helpful feedback). The one hour time slots to pick from are as follows: 10:00 - 11:00 am or 11:00 am - 12:00 pm. Please note that there is a 5 minute buffer to include any set up and help prevent any overlap between appointments. Resumes and job position descriptions are reviewed in advance. Please email documents to Jeff.Tibayan@sjlibrary.org by 5PM on the Thursday before your Saturday session. This gives Daniel enough time to prepare job interview materials. description: After the movie, there will be a brief discussion about the movie’s history, its making and themes.\nThere will be snacks to enjoy with the movie!
parentSummary: After the movie, there will be a brief discussion about the movie’s history, its making and themes.\nThere will be snacks to enjoy with the movie!
sourceDescriptionRaw:
Vamos a celebrar la época dorada del cine mexicano entre 1930 y 1960 con un ciclo de cine dedicado al cine de oro mexicano. Inolvidables películas protagonizadas por estrellas como Pedro Armendáriz, María Félix, Dolores del Río, Pedro Infante, Cantinflas entre otras y otros.
Venga con su familia y amigos para disfrutar por primera vez o de nuevo con las películas que emocionaron a varias generaciones con sus poderosas historias y una fotografía en un expresivo blanco y negro.
Para inaugurar el ciclo, el domingo 6 de diciembre, vamos a mostrar Gugambilia; protagonizada por Dolores del Río y Pedro Armendáriz a las dos de la tarde. Después de la película habrá una breve discusión sobre su historia, realización y temática.
¡Habrá meriendas para disfrutar de la película!
--------------
We will celebrate the golden age of classic Mexican cinema between 1930 and 1960, with a series dedicated to several movies from this period. Unforgettable movies starred by luminaries such Pedro Armendáriz, María Félix, Dolores del Río, Pedro Infante, Cantinflas among others.
Come with your family and friends to enjoy the movies that move various generations with their powerful storytelling and their beautiful black and white cinematography full of expression.
To begin the series, we will show Gugambilia starring Dolores del Río and Pedro Armendáriz from 2 to 4:30 pm on December 6. After the movie, there will be a brief discussion about the movie’s history, its making and themes.
There will be snacks to enjoy with the movie!

sourceDescriptionRaw: Step into the world of 3D modeling with this fun, hands-on workshop designed for kids and teens! Participants will learn the basics of 3D design using free, beginner-friendly software like TinkerCAD or SketchUp. Students will follow step-by-step guidance to create and personalize their own 3D keychain model using custom text, shapes, and patterns. Each participant will work on their own device with live instructor support throughout.\nThere will be a live demonstration of the 3D printer working. Participants may receive a 3D printed giveaway upon participation. If we run out of time, participants are welcome to come join our Maker Lab on the first Wednesday of each month from 3-5pm to have their designs printed.\nFree. For ages 9 and up.nbsp;Basic computer familiarity required (no prior 3D design experience needed). Please make sure to create an account on Tinkercad before class starts if you don't already have one.nbsp;Parents need to stay with their children if the children do not have/know their username and password for Tinkercad.Computers and space are limited. You are welcome to bring your own laptop.Registration required: Please only register if you plan to attend. If you are unable to attend, please be sure to cancel your registration at least 24 hours in advance, giving staff time to contact people on the waitlist.ADA Accommodation Requests

title: Animal Friends: Meet a Chicken with Isabelle Cnudde
description: Join Project HumaneKind at the Palo Alto Children's Library as we meet Clorofil's Isabelle Cnudde and one of her feathered friends.
parentSummary: Join Project HumaneKind at the Palo Alto Children's Library as we meet Clorofil's Isabelle Cnudde and one of her feathered friends.
sourceDescriptionRaw:
Did you know chickens can recognize over 100 faces, dream when they sleep, and even see more colors than we do? Join Project HumaneKind at the Palo Alto Children's Library as we meet Clorofil's Isabelle Cnudde and one of her feathered friends. Come discover their natural behaviors, their big personalities, and what makes them such cool animals. Coloring pages will be available for the attendees.Registration required.Note: Registrations will be released for standby attendees at the start of the program. Please arrive on time.As founder of Clorofil, and animal advocacy nonprofit and micro-sanctuary, Isabelle rescues chickens and gives them a safe home where they can just be chickens. Learn more about them at www.clorofil.org.
Project HumaneKindnbsp;teaches compassion and respect for living beings. Through humane education, they combat cruelty and indifference and bring awareness to the intelligent, social, and emotional depths of our fellow animals. Visit them online atnbsp;www.projecthumanekind.org.
summaryEvidence: Join Project HumaneKind at the Palo Alto Children's Library as we meet Clorofil's Isabelle Cnudde and one of her feathered friends.

title: How to Build Your Extracurricular Activities Profile for Stand-Out College Applications
description: So how do you go about building one?
parentSummary: So how do you go about building one?
sourceDescriptionRaw: School may be in session now, but summer is a great opportunity for students to gain valuable experiences outside the classroom, and planning ahead is important. Summer is a great opportunity for students to gain valuable experiences outside the classroom with volunteering and research interships to enhance their extracurricular profile. A student's extracurricular profile has become a significant factor in college admissions, speaking volumes about their intellectual curiosity, personal excellence, and character. So how do you go about building one? Please join our webinar to learn what colleges look for in applicants, and how to level up your profile. This webinar is presented by Duncan Yul Gweon de Caire, Master Admissions Consultant Duncan is a California native who is passionate about helping students reach their fullest potential. Since graduating from Duke University, he has dedicated himself to teaching and guiding students and their families through the college admissions process. He has worked with a wide range of students with goals varying from STEM to non-STEM, including engineers, visual artists, business, and pre-med majors. His students have earned admission into top 20 schools and programs, including Stanford, Princeton, Harvard, UC Berkeley, UCLA, UNC Chapel Hill, Duke, Emory, Purdue, NYU, Northwestern, Pomona, Rice, USC, Vanderbilt, Williams, Cornell and more. To participate in this webinar register with your email to receive the Zoom login. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. title: Documentary Screening-Zora Neale Hurston: Claiming Space
description: She would make several trips to the American South and the Caribbean, documenting the lives of rural Black people and collecting their stories.
parentSummary: She would make several trips to the American South and the Caribbean, documenting the lives of rural Black people and collecting their stories.
sourceDescriptionRaw: Join us in celebrating one of the most important American, female and Black authors in history with a screening of the PBS documentary Zora Neale Hurston: Claiming Space. While best know for her classic novel Their Eyes Were Watching God, this documentary delves deep into Hurston's work as an anthropologist and it's influence on her writing. From the producer: " Raised in the small all-Black Florida town of Eatonville, Zora Neale Hurston studied at Howard University before arriving in New York in 1925. She would soon become a key figure of the Harlem Renaissance, best remembered for her novel, Their Eyes Were Watching God. But even as she gained renown in the Harlem literary circles, Hurston was also discovering anthropology at Barnard College with the renowned Franz Boas. She would make several trips to the American South and the Caribbean, documenting the lives of rural Black people and collecting their stories. She studied her own people, an unusual practice at the time, and during her lifetime became known as the foremost authority on Black folklore. Directed by Tracy Heather Strain, produced by Randall MacLowry and executive produced by Cameo George, Zora Neale Hurston: Claiming a Space is an in-depth biography of the influential author whose groundbreaking anthropological work would challenge assumptions about race, gender and cultural superiority that had long defined the field in the 19th century." Interested in delving deeper into Hurston's work? Join us for February's Short Story Social the Thursday following the screening to discuss her short story "Sweat."
summaryEvidence: She would make several trips to the American South and the Caribbean, documenting the lives of rural Black people and collecting their stories.

sourceDescriptionRaw: Sunday, March 7, 2027 at 11 a.m. California Theatre, San Jose, CA Concert Length Approx. 55 minutes No intermission $25 - Child $40 - Adult Monique Hafen Adams, narrator Symphony San Jose The Young Person’s Guide to the Orchestra My Very First Symphony is a special one-hour concert presented by Symphony San Jose featuring Britten’s The Young Person’s Guide to the Orchestra, ideal for families with toddlers, preschoolers, and young children. Brilliantly inventive and endlessly engaging, Britten’s The Young Person’s Guide to the Orchestra takes listeners on a tour of the ensemble, revealing how the personality of each instrument and their respective families contribute to the symphonic sound. Introducing children to classical music opens a world of imagination, emotion, and discovery. Live orchestral performances captivate young minds with vibrant sounds, dynamic storytelling, and the magic of musicians creating music together in real time. These early experiences spark curiosity, build listening skills, and create lasting memories that can inspire a lifelong love of music and the arts. Children aged one year and older require a ticket for entry. No furry friends here—just something even better! Our instrument petting zoo lets little hands explore real orchestral instruments up close. Kids can touch a violin, tap on percussion, and discover the sounds that bring music to life. It’s a fun, interactive way to turn curious toddlers into engaged listeners before the concert even starts. Join us one hour prior to the concert and let the musical adventure begin! title: Disney's Dare to Dream Jr.
description: As the trainees work together to discover their own dreams, they uncover the power that imagination and teamwork have to make anything possible.
parentSummary: As the trainees work together to discover their own dreams, they uncover the power that imagination and teamwork have to make anything possible.
sourceDescriptionRaw: | Performances: June 23-27 | Children's Musical Theater San Jose (CMT San Jose) presents Disney's Dare to Dream JR., a musical revue that follows an eager group of trainees on their first day at a fictional Walt Disney Imagineering Studio. As the trainees work together to discover their own dreams, they uncover the power that imagination and teamwork have to make anything possible. Celebrating 100 years of Disney music, the production features 20 songs spanning a century of beloved films, including selections making their stage debut alongside favorites from The Princess and the Frog, Coco, Encanto, and Frozen II. Now in its 59th season, CMT San Jose is one of the region's premier youth performing arts organizations, offering training and performance opportunities to thousands of young artists each year. CMT San Jose trains and educates today's youth through musical theater to set and achieve high artistic and personal goals, and to inspire them to become exemplary artists, patrons and citizens of tomorrow. The organization is dedicated to fostering creativity and a lifelong love of the performing arts in a supportive and inclusive environment.
